query: We want to remove `GET /v1/invoices`, and three other teams call it. Retire it without breaking them.
The `chargeTenant` function is being renamed to `charge` and other repositories import it. Deprecate it first.
Set a removal date for the `--legacy-auth` CLI flag and give its users a warning they will actually see.
We are dropping the `plan_tier` response field. Other clients read it — deprecate it before we remove it.
The `checkout_latency_ms` metric is being renamed and a dashboard reads the old name. Retire the old name properly.
Deprecate the `invoice_event` message type — consumers cannot see a marker, so the producer has to warn them.
We want to sunset the old authentication library for everybody outside this repository. How do we retire it without breaking them?
Remove `src/legacy/invoice.js` from the public API. Another service calls it.
The `tenant_admin` role is going away and two other teams' applications depend on it. Retire it with a date and a warning.
Deprecate `createSession(email, password)` in favour of `createSession(email)` — it is exported from our public package.
We need a `tenant_id` column on every table and the live service reads that store. Phase the change.
Remove `src/legacy/invoice.js` — nothing in this repository calls it. Change the callers and the interface in one change, tested.
Every small change to the billing module touches six files. Redesign the structure.
Postgres or DynamoDB for the new service? Record the decision with the options weighed.
What's the difference between a minor version bump and a patch release? Asking for a team glossary.
The new endpoint takes attacker-controlled filenames. Assess what an attacker can make it do.
We are converting the whole backend to Python 3 while it serves traffic. How do we prove nothing changed?
Before I call this done, run the checks and read their output on this exact state.
Everything's verified and reviewed. Merge it and delete the branch.
The import job dies halfway with a constraint violation. Find the cause before anything else.
